task.objective: Audit the reporting period's ledger against the source documents and the policy. Report every discrepancy of the four finding types with evidence, then call submit exactly once. Some ledgers are clean: an empty findings list is the correct answer when nothing is wrong.

duplicate_invoice.meaning: The same invoice, purchase or sales, is posted twice, possibly keyed again on a later date (see policy.duplicate_rule).
duplicate_invoice.amount: base amount posted for the later copy (equal for two copies with the same issued_at instant)
duplicate_invoice.evidence: both invoice documents plus, for both copies, the posting row on the same side (both payable/receivable rows, or both expense/revenue rows)

unallocated_payment.meaning: A receipt references an invoice whose open balance covers it, yet part or all of it is credited to 2900 instead of relieving the invoice.
unallocated_payment.evidence: the payment document, the invoice document, the payment's 2900 row, and every ledger row of the invoice on its receivable account 1100: its posting (or opening item) and every relief, by earlier payments that left the balance and by this payment; for a foreign-currency invoice also the payment's bank (1000) row

wrong_fx_rate.meaning: A foreign-currency document is converted with a rate other than the policy rate (wrong date or wrong value). The policy rate follows the document's own date, not the moment it was posted.
wrong_fx_rate.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_fx_rate.amount: absolute difference between the posted base amount and the policy base amount, measured on the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_fx_rate.evidence: the document, the posting row (invoices: either side; payments: bank row), and the fx record of the correct date

wrong_period.meaning: A document is posted outside the period its own timestamp belongs to, in company time; only crossings into or out of the reporting period count. A posting at another moment inside the document's own period is ordinary (policy.posting_rules.posting_timestamp) and is no finding.
wrong_period.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_period.amount: posted base amount of the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_period.evidence: the document and one of its posting rows (invoices: either side; payments: the bank row)

conventions.amounts: claimed_amount_minor is a non-negative integer in minor units of the base currency; currency is the base currency code
conventions.ids: affected_ids and evidence_ids are compared as sets after trimming spaces (case-sensitive). A document may be cited by doc_id or by its invoice_id/payment_id. FX records are cited as 'YYYY-MM-DD:SRC:TGT'. A finding needs at least one complete evidence set; extra well-formed IDs are ignored. Every ID must be a non-blank string of at most max_id_chars characters; a submission with a malformed ID is rejected as invalid.
conventions.matching: one-to-one with the answer key; repeated or unmatched findings are false positives

reward.inspection_steps: every step except the final submit

get_document.doc_id: doc_id of an invoice or payment

calculator.expression: arithmetic on decimal numbers: + - * / and parentheses; at most 256 characters and at most 200 tokens (each number, operator and parenthesis is one token)

policy.local_time_rule: Company-local time of an instant = the instant plus the UTC offset in force at that instant, taken from utc_offset_schedule (each entry applies from its from_utc instant until the next entry). Local calendar dates are always taken in company time, whatever offset a timestamp happens to be written with.

reporting_period.rule: A document belongs to the reporting period when start <= its own timestamp < end, compared as instants (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). A posting belongs to the period of its ledger timestamp. A posting must fall in the same period as its document.

ledger_extract.rule: ledger.csv covers the reporting period plus a 7-day cut-off window after it. Items open at period start are carried in by opening journals dated at period start against account 3900.

fx.date_rule: Use the rate dated on the document's local calendar date (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). If no rate is published on that date, use the latest earlier published date.
fx.other_pairs: Rows for pairs other than document currency -> base currency are not used for postings.

posting_rules.posting_timestamp: A posting is booked at its own moment, which may be earlier or later than its document's timestamp (minutes, hours or days). That moment must fall in the same reporting period as the document (see reporting_period.rule). It never changes an amount: amounts and exchange rates follow the document (its local calendar date under fx.date_rule), never the posting moment.
posting_rules.sales_invoice: Dr 1100 / Cr 4000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.purchase_invoice: Dr 5000 / Cr 2000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.receipt: Dr 1000 for the base amount at the payment-date rate. Allocate the payment to invoice_refs in the listed order, each up to its open balance in document currency. Relieve 1100 at the booked carrying amount: proportional to the allocated share of the open document amount, and the allocation that closes an item relieves its whole remaining carrying amount. Any remainder beyond the referenced open balances (an invoice that is not yet posted when the receipt is booked, or that earlier payments have already settled, has none), or the whole receipt when invoice_refs is null, is credited to 2900 at the payment-date rate. The balancing difference is posted to 7900.
posting_rules.disbursement: Dr 2000 at the carrying amount relieved, Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.refund: A refund references the invoice whose overpayment it returns. Dr 2900 at the carrying amount of that overpayment credit (proportional if partly refunded), Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.payment_currency: A payment is in the currency of every invoice it references.
posting_rules.opening: One opening journal per open invoice (keyed by invoice_id) and one bank opening journal without IDs, all dated at period start.

policy.journal_grouping: Ledger rows form one journal when they share payment_id; otherwise when they share invoice_id; otherwise when their timestamps denote the same instant (compare as instants, whatever offset each timestamp is written with; never compare the timestamp strings literally).
policy.duplicate_rule: Two invoices are duplicates when kind, entity_id, currency, total_minor and every line item (description, quantity, unit_price_minor, amount_minor, ref) are identical. Line refs identify the supply: the supplier's references on purchase invoices and the delivery references on sales invoices. issued_at need not be identical: a copy keyed again later carries the later issued_at and is converted at the rate of its own local date. Invoices that differ in any line ref are separate supplies, even with the same counterparty, date, lines and amount. The duplicate amount is the base amount posted for the later copy; compare issued_at values as instants, whatever offset each is written with; two copies of the same instant post equal amounts.
policy.nulls: Missing references are explicit nulls: an empty field in CSV, null in JSON. Links are never guessed.

policy.local_time_rule: Company-local time of an instant = the instant plus the UTC offset in force at that instant, taken from utc_offset_schedule (each entry applies from its from_utc instant until the next entry). Local calendar dates are always taken in company time, whatever offset a timestamp happens to be written with.

reporting_period.rule: A document belongs to the reporting period when start <= its own timestamp < end, compared as instants (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). A posting belongs to the period of its ledger timestamp. A posting must fall in the same period as its document.

ledger_extract.rule: ledger.csv covers the reporting period plus a 7-day cut-off window after it. Items open at period start are carried in by opening journals dated at period start against account 3900.

fx.date_rule: Use the rate dated on the document's local calendar date (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). If no rate is published on that date, use the latest earlier published date.
fx.other_pairs: Rows for pairs other than document currency -> base currency are not used for postings.

posting_rules.posting_timestamp: A posting is booked at its own moment, which may be earlier or later than its document's timestamp (minutes, hours or days). That moment must fall in the same reporting period as the document (see reporting_period.rule). It never changes an amount: amounts and exchange rates follow the document (its local calendar date under fx.date_rule), never the posting moment.
posting_rules.sales_invoice: Dr 1100 / Cr 4000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.purchase_invoice: Dr 5000 / Cr 2000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.receipt: Dr 1000 for the base amount at the payment-date rate. Allocate the payment to invoice_refs in the listed order, each up to its open balance in document currency. Relieve 1100 at the booked carrying amount: proportional to the allocated share of the open document amount, and the allocation that closes an item relieves its whole remaining carrying amount. Any remainder beyond the referenced open balances (an invoice that is not yet posted when the receipt is booked, or that earlier payments have already settled, has none), or the whole receipt when invoice_refs is null, is credited to 2900 at the payment-date rate. The balancing difference is posted to 7900.
posting_rules.disbursement: Dr 2000 at the carrying amount relieved, Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.refund: A refund references the invoice whose overpayment it returns. Dr 2900 at the carrying amount of that overpayment credit (proportional if partly refunded), Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.payment_currency: A payment is in the currency of every invoice it references.
posting_rules.opening: One opening journal per open invoice (keyed by invoice_id) and one bank opening journal without IDs, all dated at period start.

policy.journal_grouping: Ledger rows form one journal when they share payment_id; otherwise when they share invoice_id; otherwise when their timestamps denote the same instant (compare as instants, whatever offset each timestamp is written with; never compare the timestamp strings literally).
policy.duplicate_rule: Two invoices are duplicates when kind, entity_id, currency, total_minor and every line item (description, quantity, unit_price_minor, amount_minor, ref) are identical. Line refs identify the supply: the supplier's references on purchase invoices and the delivery references on sales invoices. issued_at need not be identical: a copy keyed again later carries the later issued_at and is converted at the rate of its own local date. Invoices that differ in any line ref are separate supplies, even with the same counterparty, date, lines and amount. The duplicate amount is the base amount posted for the later copy; compare issued_at values as instants, whatever offset each is written with; two copies of the same instant post equal amounts.
policy.nulls: Missing references are explicit nulls: an empty field in CSV, null in JSON. Links are never guessed.

task.objective: Audit the reporting period's ledger against the source documents and the policy. Report every discrepancy of the four finding types with evidence, then call submit exactly once. Some ledgers are clean: an empty findings list is the correct answer when nothing is wrong.

duplicate_invoice.meaning: The same invoice, purchase or sales, is posted twice, possibly keyed again on a later date (see policy.duplicate_rule).
duplicate_invoice.amount: base amount posted for the later copy (equal for two copies with the same issued_at instant)
duplicate_invoice.evidence: both invoice documents plus, for both copies, the posting row on the same side (both payable/receivable rows, or both expense/revenue rows)

unallocated_payment.meaning: A receipt references an invoice whose open balance covers it, yet part or all of it is credited to 2900 instead of relieving the invoice.
unallocated_payment.evidence: the payment document, the invoice document, the payment's 2900 row, and every ledger row of the invoice on its receivable account 1100: its posting (or opening item) and every relief, by earlier payments that left the balance and by this payment; for a foreign-currency invoice also the payment's bank (1000) row

wrong_fx_rate.meaning: A foreign-currency document is converted with a rate other than the policy rate (wrong date or wrong value). The policy rate follows the document's own date, not the moment it was posted.
wrong_fx_rate.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_fx_rate.amount: absolute difference between the posted base amount and the policy base amount, measured on the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_fx_rate.evidence: the document, the posting row (invoices: either side; payments: bank row), and the fx record of the correct date

wrong_period.meaning: A document is posted outside the period its own timestamp belongs to, in company time; only crossings into or out of the reporting period count. A posting at another moment inside the document's own period is ordinary (policy.posting_rules.posting_timestamp) and is no finding.
wrong_period.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_period.amount: posted base amount of the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_period.evidence: the document and one of its posting rows (invoices: either side; payments: the bank row)

conventions.amounts: claimed_amount_minor is a non-negative integer in minor units of the base currency; currency is the base currency code
conventions.ids: affected_ids and evidence_ids are compared as sets after trimming spaces (case-sensitive). A document may be cited by doc_id or by its invoice_id/payment_id. FX records are cited as 'YYYY-MM-DD:SRC:TGT'. A finding needs at least one complete evidence set; extra well-formed IDs are ignored. Every ID must be a non-blank string of at most max_id_chars characters; a submission with a malformed ID is rejected as invalid.
conventions.matching: one-to-one with the answer key; repeated or unmatched findings are false positives

reward.inspection_steps: every step except the final submit

ledger_extract.rule: ledger.csv covers the reporting period plus a 7-day cut-off window after it. Items open at period start are carried in by opening journals dated at period start against account 3900.

fx.other_pairs: Rows for pairs other than document currency -> base currency are not used for postings.

posting_rules.sales_invoice: Dr 1100 / Cr 4000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.purchase_invoice: Dr 5000 / Cr 2000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.receipt: Dr 1000 for the base amount at the payment-date rate. Allocate the payment to invoice_refs in the listed order, each up to its open balance in document currency. posting_rules.disbursement: Dr 2000 at the carrying amount relieved, Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.

reporting_period.rule: A document belongs to the reporting period when start <= its own timestamp < end, compared as instants (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). A posting belongs to the period of its ledger timestamp. A posting must fall in the same period as its document.

ledger_extract.rule: ledger.csv covers the reporting period plus a 7-day cut-off window after it. Items open at period start are carried in by opening journals dated at period start against account 3900.

fx.date_rule: Use the rate dated on the document's local calendar date (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). If no rate is published on that date, use the latest earlier published date.
fx.other_pairs: Rows for pairs other than document currency -> base currency are not used for postings.

posting_rules.posting_timestamp: A posting is booked at its own moment, which may be earlier or later than its document's timestamp (minutes, hours or days). posting_rules.sales_invoice: Dr 1100 / Cr 4000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.purchase_invoice: Dr 5000 / Cr 2000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.receipt: Dr 1000 for the base amount at the payment-date rate. Allocate the payment to invoice_refs in the listed order, each up to its open balance in document currency. Relieve 1100 at the booked carrying amount: proportional to the allocated share of the open document amount, and the allocation that closes an item relieves its whole remaining carrying amount. Any remainder beyond the referenced open balances (an invoice that is not yet posted when the receipt is booked, or that earlier payments have already settled, has none), or the whole receipt when invoice_refs is null, is credited to 2900 at the payment-date rate. posting_rules.disbursement: Dr 2000 at the carrying amount relieved, Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.refund: A refund references the invoice whose overpayment it returns. Dr 2900 at the carrying amount of that overpayment credit (proportional if partly refunded), Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.payment_currency: A payment is in the currency of every invoice it references.

reporting_period.rule: A document belongs to the reporting period when start <= its own timestamp < end, compared as instants (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). A posting belongs to the period of its ledger timestamp. A posting must fall in the same period as its document.

ledger_extract.rule: ledger.csv covers the reporting period plus a 7-day cut-off window after it. Items open at period start are carried in by opening journals dated at period start against account 3900.

fx.date_rule: Use the rate dated on the document's local calendar date (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). If no rate is published on that date, use the latest earlier published date.
fx.other_pairs: Rows for pairs other than document currency -> base currency are not used for postings.

posting_rules.posting_timestamp: A posting is booked at its own moment, which may be earlier or later than its document's timestamp (minutes, hours or days). posting_rules.sales_invoice: Dr 1100 / Cr 4000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.purchase_invoice: Dr 5000 / Cr 2000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.receipt: Dr 1000 for the base amount at the payment-date rate. Allocate the payment to invoice_refs in the listed order, each up to its open balance in document currency. Relieve 1100 at the booked carrying amount: proportional to the allocated share of the open document amount, and the allocation that closes an item relieves its whole remaining carrying amount. Any remainder beyond the referenced open balances (an invoice that is not yet posted when the receipt is booked, or that earlier payments have already settled, has none), or the whole receipt when invoice_refs is null, is credited to 2900 at the payment-date rate. The balancing difference is posted to 7900.
posting_rules.disbursement: Dr 2000 at the carrying amount relieved, Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.refund: A refund references the invoice whose overpayment it returns. Dr 2900 at the carrying amount of that overpayment credit (proportional if partly refunded), Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.payment_currency: A payment is in the currency of every invoice it references.
posting_rules.opening: One opening journal per open invoice (keyed by invoice_id) and one bank opening journal without IDs, all dated at period start.

policy.journal_grouping: Ledger rows form one journal when they share payment_id; otherwise when they share invoice_id; otherwise when their timestamps denote the same instant (compare as instants, whatever offset each timestamp is written with; never compare the timestamp strings literally).

Invoices that differ in any line ref are separate supplies, even with the same counterparty, date, lines and amount. The duplicate amount is the base amount posted for the later copy; compare issued_at values as instants, whatever offset each is written with; two copies of the same instant post equal amounts.

posting_rules.receipt: Dr 1000 for the base amount at the payment-date rate. Allocate the payment to invoice_refs in the listed order, each up to its open balance in document currency. Relieve 1100 at the booked carrying amount: proportional to the allocated share of the open document amount, and the allocation that closes an item relieves its whole remaining carrying amount. Any remainder beyond the referenced open balances (an invoice that is not yet posted when the receipt is booked, or that earlier payments have already settled, has none), or the whole receipt when invoice_refs is null, is credited to 2900 at the payment-date rate. The balancing difference is posted to 7900.
posting_rules.disbursement: Dr 2000 at the carrying amount relieved, Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.refund: A refund references the invoice whose overpayment it returns. Dr 2900 at the carrying amount of that overpayment credit (proportional if partly refunded), Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.payment_currency: A payment is in the currency of every invoice it references.

policy.journal_grouping: Ledger rows form one journal when they share payment_id; otherwise when they share invoice_id; otherwise when their timestamps denote the same instant (compare as instants, whatever offset each timestamp is written with; never compare the timestamp strings literally).
policy.duplicate_rule: Two invoices are duplicates when kind, entity_id, currency, total_minor and every line item (description, quantity, unit_price_minor, amount_minor, ref) are identical. Invoices that differ in any line ref are separate supplies, even with the same counterparty, date, lines and amount. The duplicate amount is the base amount posted for the later copy; compare issued_at values as instants, whatever offset each is written with; two copies of the same instant post equal amounts.

task.objective: Audit the reporting period's ledger against the source documents and the policy. Report every discrepancy of the four finding types with evidence, then call submit exactly once. Some ledgers are clean: an empty findings list is the correct answer when nothing is wrong.

duplicate_invoice.meaning: The same invoice, purchase or sales, is posted twice, possibly keyed again on a later date (see policy.duplicate_rule).
duplicate_invoice.amount: base amount posted for the later copy (equal for two copies with the same issued_at instant)
duplicate_invoice.evidence: both invoice documents plus, for both copies, the posting row on the same side (both payable/receivable rows, or both expense/revenue rows)

unallocated_payment.meaning: A receipt references an invoice whose open balance covers it, yet part or all of it is credited to 2900 instead of relieving the invoice.
unallocated_payment.evidence: the payment document, the invoice document, the payment's 2900 row, and every ledger row of the invoice on its receivable account 1100: its posting (or opening item) and every relief, by earlier payments that left the balance and by this payment; for a foreign-currency invoice also the payment's bank (1000) row

wrong_fx_rate.meaning: A foreign-currency document is converted with a rate other than the policy rate (wrong date or wrong value). The policy rate follows the document's own date, not the moment it was posted.
wrong_fx_rate.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_fx_rate.amount: absolute difference between the posted base amount and the policy base amount, measured on the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_fx_rate.evidence: the document, the posting row (invoices: either side; payments: bank row), and the fx record of the correct date

wrong_period.meaning: A document is posted outside the period its own timestamp belongs to, in company time; only crossings into or out of the reporting period count. A posting at another moment inside the document's own period is ordinary (policy.posting_rules.posting_timestamp) and is no finding.
wrong_period.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_period.amount: posted base amount of the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_period.evidence: the document and one of its posting rows (invoices: either side; payments: the bank row)

conventions.amounts: claimed_amount_minor is a non-negative integer in minor units of the base currency; currency is the base currency code
conventions.ids: affected_ids and evidence_ids are compared as sets after trimming spaces (case-sensitive). A document may be cited by doc_id or by its invoice_id/payment_id. FX records are cited as 'YYYY-MM-DD:SRC:TGT'. A finding needs at least one complete evidence set; extra well-formed IDs are ignored. Every ID must be a non-blank string of at most max_id_chars characters; a submission with a malformed ID is rejected as invalid.
conventions.matching: one-to-one with the answer key; repeated or unmatched findings are false positives

policy.local_time_rule: Company-local time of an instant = the instant plus the UTC offset in force at that instant, taken from utc_offset_schedule (each entry applies from its from_utc instant until the next entry). reporting_period.rule: A document belongs to the reporting period when start <= its own timestamp < end, compared as instants (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). A posting belongs to the period of its ledger timestamp. A posting must fall in the same period as its document.

ledger_extract.rule: ledger.csv covers the reporting period plus a 7-day cut-off window after it. Items open at period start are carried in by opening journals dated at period start against account 3900.

fx.date_rule: Use the rate dated on the document's local calendar date (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). If no rate is published on that date, use the latest earlier published date.
fx.other_pairs: Rows for pairs other than document currency -> base currency are not used for postings.

posting_rules.posting_timestamp: A posting is booked at its own moment, which may be earlier or later than its document's timestamp (minutes, hours or days). That moment must fall in the same reporting period as the document (see reporting_period.rule). It never changes an amount: amounts and exchange rates follow the document (its local calendar date under fx.date_rule), never the posting moment.
posting_rules.sales_invoice: Dr 1100 / Cr 4000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.purchase_invoice: Dr 5000 / Cr 2000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.receipt: Dr 1000 for the base amount at the payment-date rate. Allocate the payment to invoice_refs in the listed order, each up to its open balance in document currency. Relieve 1100 at the booked carrying amount: proportional to the allocated share of the open document amount, and the allocation that closes an item relieves its whole remaining carrying amount. Any remainder beyond the referenced open balances (an invoice that is not yet posted when the receipt is booked, or that earlier payments have already settled, has none), or the whole receipt when invoice_refs is null, is credited to 2900 at the payment-date rate. The balancing difference is posted to 7900.
posting_rules.disbursement: Dr 2000 at the carrying amount relieved, Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.refund: A refund references the invoice whose overpayment it returns. Dr 2900 at the carrying amount of that overpayment credit (proportional if partly refunded), Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.payment_currency: A payment is in the currency of every invoice it references.
posting_rules.opening: One opening journal per open invoice (keyed by invoice_id) and one bank opening journal without IDs, all dated at period start.

policy.journal_grouping: Ledger rows form one journal when they share payment_id; otherwise when they share invoice_id; otherwise when their timestamps denote the same instant (compare as instants, whatever offset each timestamp is written with; never compare the timestamp strings literally).
policy.duplicate_rule: Two invoices are duplicates when kind, entity_id, currency, total_minor and every line item (description, quantity, unit_price_minor, amount_minor, ref) are identical. Line refs identify the supply: the supplier's references on purchase invoices and the delivery references on sales invoices. issued_at need not be identical: a copy keyed again later carries the later issued_at and is converted at the rate of its own local date. Invoices that differ in any line ref are separate supplies, even with the same counterparty, date, lines and amount. The duplicate amount is the base amount posted for the later copy; compare issued_at values as instants, whatever offset each is written with; two copies of the same instant post equal amounts.

fx.other_pairs: Rows for pairs other than document currency -> base currency are not used for postings.

posting_rules.purchase_invoice: Dr 5000 / Cr 2000 for the base amount of total_minor.

reporting_period.rule: A document belongs to the reporting period when start <= its own timestamp < end, compared as instants (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). A posting belongs to the period of its ledger timestamp. A posting must fall in the same period as its document.

ledger_extract.rule: ledger.csv covers the reporting period plus a 7-day cut-off window after it. Items open at period start are carried in by opening journals dated at period start against account 3900.

fx.date_rule: Use the rate dated on the document's local calendar date (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). If no rate is published on that date, use the latest earlier published date.
fx.other_pairs: Rows for pairs other than document currency -> base currency are not used for postings.

posting_rules.posting_timestamp: A posting is booked at its own moment, which may be earlier or later than its document's timestamp (minutes, hours or days). That moment must fall in the same reporting period as the document (see reporting_period.rule). It never changes an amount: amounts and exchange rates follow the document (its local calendar date under fx.date_rule), never the posting moment.
posting_rules.sales_invoice: Dr 1100 / Cr 4000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.purchase_invoice: Dr 5000 / Cr 2000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.receipt: Dr 1000 for the base amount at the payment-date rate. Allocate the payment to invoice_refs in the listed order, each up to its open balance in document currency. Relieve 1100 at the booked carrying amount: proportional to the allocated share of the open document amount, and the allocation that closes an item relieves its whole remaining carrying amount. Any remainder beyond the referenced open balances (an invoice that is not yet posted when the receipt is booked, or that earlier payments have already settled, has none), or the whole receipt when invoice_refs is null, is credited to 2900 at the payment-date rate. The balancing difference is posted to 7900.
posting_rules.disbursement: Dr 2000 at the carrying amount relieved, Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.refund: A refund references the invoice whose overpayment it returns. Dr 2900 at the carrying amount of that overpayment credit (proportional if partly refunded), Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.payment_currency: A payment is in the currency of every invoice it references.
posting_rules.opening: One opening journal per open invoice (keyed by invoice_id) and one bank opening journal without IDs, all dated at period start.

policy.journal_grouping: Ledger rows form one journal when they share payment_id; otherwise when they share invoice_id; otherwise when their timestamps denote the same instant (compare as instants, whatever offset each timestamp is written with; never compare the timestamp strings literally).
policy.duplicate_rule: Two invoices are duplicates when kind, entity_id, currency, total_minor and every line item (description, quantity, unit_price_minor, amount_minor, ref) are identical. Line refs identify the supply: the supplier's references on purchase invoices and the delivery references on sales invoices. issued_at need not be identical: a copy keyed again later carries the later issued_at and is converted at the rate of its own local date. Invoices that differ in any line ref are separate supplies, even with the same counterparty, date, lines and amount. The duplicate amount is the base amount posted for the later copy; compare issued_at values as instants, whatever offset each is written with; two copies of the same instant post equal amounts.
policy.nulls: Missing references are explicit nulls: an empty field in CSV, null in JSON. Links are never guessed.

task.objective: Audit the reporting period's ledger against the source documents and the policy. Report every discrepancy of the four finding types with evidence, then call submit exactly once. Some ledgers are clean: an empty findings list is the correct answer when nothing is wrong.

duplicate_invoice.meaning: The same invoice, purchase or sales, is posted twice, possibly keyed again on a later date (see policy.duplicate_rule).
duplicate_invoice.amount: base amount posted for the later copy (equal for two copies with the same issued_at instant)
duplicate_invoice.evidence: both invoice documents plus, for both copies, the posting row on the same side (both payable/receivable rows, or both expense/revenue rows)

unallocated_payment.meaning: A receipt references an invoice whose open balance covers it, yet part or all of it is credited to 2900 instead of relieving the invoice.
unallocated_payment.evidence: the payment document, the invoice document, the payment's 2900 row, and every ledger row of the invoice on its receivable account 1100: its posting (or opening item) and every relief, by earlier payments that left the balance and by this payment; for a foreign-currency invoice also the payment's bank (1000) row

wrong_fx_rate.meaning: A foreign-currency document is converted with a rate other than the policy rate (wrong date or wrong value). The policy rate follows the document's own date, not the moment it was posted.
wrong_fx_rate.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_fx_rate.amount: absolute difference between the posted base amount and the policy base amount, measured on the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_fx_rate.evidence: the document, the posting row (invoices: either side; payments: bank row), and the fx record of the correct date

wrong_period.meaning: A document is posted outside the period its own timestamp belongs to, in company time; only crossings into or out of the reporting period count. A posting at another moment inside the document's own period is ordinary (policy.posting_rules.posting_timestamp) and is no finding.
wrong_period.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_period.amount: posted base amount of the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_period.evidence: the document and one of its posting rows (invoices: either side; payments: the bank row)

conventions.amounts: claimed_amount_minor is a non-negative integer in minor units of the base currency; currency is the base currency code
conventions.ids: affected_ids and evidence_ids are compared as sets after trimming spaces (case-sensitive). A document may be cited by doc_id or by its invoice_id/payment_id. FX records are cited as 'YYYY-MM-DD:SRC:TGT'. A finding needs at least one complete evidence set; extra well-formed IDs are ignored. Every ID must be a non-blank string of at most max_id_chars characters; a submission with a malformed ID is rejected as invalid.
conventions.matching: one-to-one with the answer key; repeated or unmatched findings are false positives

policy.duplicate_rule: Two invoices are duplicates when kind, entity_id, currency, total_minor and every line item (description, quantity, unit_price_minor, amount_minor, ref) are identical. Line refs identify the supply: the supplier's references on purchase invoices and the delivery references on sales invoices. issued_at need not be identical: a copy keyed again later carries the later issued_at and is converted at the rate of its own local date. Invoices that differ in any line ref are separate supplies, even with the same counterparty, date, lines and amount. The duplicate amount is the base amount posted for the later copy; compare issued_at values as instants, whatever offset each is written with; two copies of the same instant post equal amounts.
policy.nulls: Missing references are explicit nulls: an empty field in CSV, null in JSON. Links are never guessed.

task.objective: Audit the reporting period's ledger against the source documents and the policy. Report every discrepancy of the four finding types with evidence, then call submit exactly once. Some ledgers are clean: an empty findings list is the correct answer when nothing is wrong.

duplicate_invoice.meaning: The same invoice, purchase or sales, is posted twice, possibly keyed again on a later date (see policy.duplicate_rule).
duplicate_invoice.amount: base amount posted for the later copy (equal for two copies with the same issued_at instant)
duplicate_invoice.evidence: both invoice documents plus, for both copies, the posting row on the same side (both payable/receivable rows, or both expense/revenue rows)

unallocated_payment.meaning: A receipt references an invoice whose open balance covers it, yet part or all of it is credited to 2900 instead of relieving the invoice.
unallocated_payment.evidence: the payment document, the invoice document, the payment's 2900 row, and every ledger row of the invoice on its receivable account 1100: its posting (or opening item) and every relief, by earlier payments that left the balance and by this payment; for a foreign-currency invoice also the payment's bank (1000) row

wrong_fx_rate.meaning: A foreign-currency document is converted with a rate other than the policy rate (wrong date or wrong value). The policy rate follows the document's own date, not the moment it was posted.
wrong_fx_rate.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_fx_rate.amount: absolute difference between the posted base amount and the policy base amount, measured on the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_fx_rate.evidence: the document, the posting row (invoices: either side; payments: bank row), and the fx record of the correct date

wrong_period.meaning: A document is posted outside the period its own timestamp belongs to, in company time; only crossings into or out of the reporting period count. A posting at another moment inside the document's own period is ordinary (policy.posting_rules.posting_timestamp) and is no finding.
wrong_period.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_period.amount: posted base amount of the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_period.evidence: the document and one of its posting rows (invoices: either side; payments: the bank row)

conventions.amounts: claimed_amount_minor is a non-negative integer in minor units of the base currency; currency is the base currency code
conventions.ids: affected_ids and evidence_ids are compared as sets after trimming spaces (case-sensitive). A document may be cited by doc_id or by its invoice_id/payment_id. FX records are cited as 'YYYY-MM-DD:SRC:TGT'. A finding needs at least one complete evidence set; extra well-formed IDs are ignored. Every ID must be a non-blank string of at most max_id_chars characters; a submission with a malformed ID is rejected as invalid.
conventions.matching: one-to-one with the answer key; repeated or unmatched findings are false positives

reward.inspection_steps: every step except the final submit
